name: addshape
doc: Add a turtle shape to the TurtleScreen’s shape list. It can be called in four different ways:

changed.text: Added support for PNG, PGM, and PPM image formats. Both a shape name and an image file name can be specified.

name: back
doc: Move the turtle backward by distance, opposite to the direction the turtle is headed. The turtle’s heading does not change.

name: backward
doc: Move the turtle backward by distance, opposite to the direction the turtle is headed. The turtle’s heading does not change.

name: begin_fill
doc: To be called just before drawing a shape to be filled.

name: begin_poly
doc: Start recording the vertices of a polygon. The current turtle position is the first vertex of the polygon.

name: bgcolor
doc: Return or set the background color of the TurtleScreen.

name: bgpic
doc: Set background image or return name of current backgroundimage. If picname is a filename, set the corresponding image as background. If picname is "nopic", delete background image, if present. If picname is None, return the filename of the current backgroundimage.

name: bk
doc: Move the turtle backward by distance, opposite to the direction the turtle is headed. The turtle’s heading does not change.

name: bye
doc: Close the turtle graphics window.

name: circle
doc: Draw a circle with the given radius. The center is radius units left of the turtle; extent, an angle, determines which part of the circle is drawn. If extent is not given, draw the entire circle. If extent is not a full circle, one endpoint of the arc is the current pen position. Draw the arc in counterclockwise direction if radius is positive, otherwise in clockwise direction. Finally, the turtle’s heading is changed by extent.

name: clear
doc: Delete the turtle’s drawings from the screen. The state and position of the turtle as well as the drawings of other turtles are not affected.

name: clearscreen
doc: Delete all drawings and all turtles from the TurtleScreen. Reset the now empty TurtleScreen to its initial state: white background, no background image, no event bindings and tracing on.

name: clearstamp
doc: Delete stamp with given stampid.

name: clearstamps
doc: Delete all or first/last n of turtle’s stamps. If n is None, delete all stamps, if n > 0 delete first n stamps, else if n < 0 delete last n stamps.

name: clone
doc: Create and return a clone of the turtle. The clone has the same position, heading and turtle properties.

name: color
doc: Return or set the pencolor and fillcolor.

name: colormode
doc: Return the colormode or set it to 1.0 or 255. After setting it, the r, g and b values of color triples have to be between 0 and cmode.

name: degrees
doc: Set the angle measurement units to degrees. The number of degrees in a full circle is set to fullcircle, which defaults to 360.

name: delay
doc: Return or set the drawing delay in milliseconds. This is approximately the time interval between two consecutive canvas updates. The longer the drawing delay, the slower the animation.

name: distance
doc: Return the distance from the turtle to (x,y) in turtle step units. If y is None, x must be a pair of coordinates, a Vec2D, for example as returned by pos(), or another turtle.

name: done
doc: Start the event loop by calling Tkinter’s mainloop() method. Must be the last statement in a turtle graphics program. Must not be used if a script is run from within IDLE in -n mode (see Running without a subprocess).

name: dot
doc: Draw a circular dot with diameter size, using color. If size is not given, the larger of pensize + 4 and 2 * pensize is used. If color is not given, the current pencolor is used.

name: down
doc: Lower the pen. The turtle draws a line when it moves.

name: end_fill
doc: Fill the shape drawn after the last call to begin_fill().

name: end_poly
doc: Stop recording the vertices of a polygon. The current turtle position is the last vertex of the polygon. This will be connected with the first vertex.

name: exitonclick
doc: Bind bye() method to mouse clicks on the Screen.

name: fd
doc: Move the turtle forward by the specified distance, in the direction the turtle is headed.

name: fill
doc: Fill the shape drawn in the with turtle.fill(): block.

name: fillcolor
doc: Return or set the fillcolor.

name: filling
doc: Return True if the turtle is filling, False otherwise.

name: forward
doc: Move the turtle forward by the specified distance, in the direction the turtle is headed.

name: get_poly
doc: Return the last recorded polygon.

name: get_shapepoly
doc: Return the current shape polygon as tuple of coordinate pairs. This can be used to define a new shape or components of a compound shape.

name: getcanvas
doc: Return the Canvas of this TurtleScreen. Useful for insiders who know what to do with a Tkinter Canvas.

name: getpen
doc: Return the Turtle object itself.

name: getscreen
doc: Return the TurtleScreen object the turtle is drawing on. TurtleScreen methods can then be called for that object.

name: getshapes
doc: Return a list of names of all currently available turtle shapes.

name: getturtle
doc: Return the Turtle object itself.

name: goto
doc: Move the turtle to an absolute position. If y is None, x must be a pair of coordinates or a Vec2D, for example as returned by pos(). If the pen is down, a line is drawn. The turtle’s heading does not change.

name: heading
doc: Return the turtle’s current heading. The value depends on the turtle mode, see mode().

name: hideturtle
doc: Make the turtle invisible. If the pen is down, movement still draws.

name: home
doc: Move the turtle to the origin, coordinates (0,0). The turtle’s heading is set to its start orientation, which depends on the turtle mode, see mode().

name: ht
doc: Make the turtle invisible. If the pen is down, movement still draws.

name: isdown
doc: Return True if the pen is down, False if it’s up.

name: isvisible
doc: Return True if the turtle is visible, False if it’s hidden.

name: left
doc: Turn the turtle left by the specified angle. The angle is measured in degrees by default; the unit can be changed with degrees() or radians(). How the heading is measured depends on the turtle mode, see mode().

name: listen
doc: Set focus on TurtleScreen (in order to collect key-events). Dummy arguments are provided in order to be able to pass listen() to the onclick method.

name: lt
doc: Turn the turtle left by the specified angle. The angle is measured in degrees by default; the unit can be changed with degrees() or radians(). How the heading is measured depends on the turtle mode, see mode().

name: mainloop
doc: Start the event loop by calling Tkinter’s mainloop() method. Must be the last statement in a turtle graphics program. Must not be used if a script is run from within IDLE in -n mode (see Running without a subprocess).

name: mode
doc: Set the turtle mode and perform a reset. mode is one of the strings “standard”, “logo” or “world”. If mode is not given, return the current mode.

name: no_animation
doc: Temporarily turn off turtle animation. The code inside the with block is not animated. Once the block is exited, the drawing appears. This is useful for drawing complex shapes where even the fastest speed setting is too slow.

name: numinput
doc: Pop up a dialog window for input of a number. title is the title of the dialog window and prompt is a text describing what numerical information to input. default is the default value, minval and maxval are the minimum and maximum values for input. If these are given, the number entered must be between minval and maxval. If not, a hint is issued and the dialog remains open for correction. Return the number entered. If the dialog is canceled, return None.

name: onclick
doc: Bind fun to mouse-click events on this screen. fun is called with the coordinates of the clicked point on the canvas. If fun is None, existing bindings are removed. btn is the number of the mouse button and defaults to 1, the left mouse button. If add is True, a new binding is added, otherwise it replaces a former binding.

name: ondrag
doc: Bind fun to mouse-move events on this turtle. If fun is None, existing bindings are removed.

name: onkey
doc: Bind fun to key-release event of key. If fun is None, event bindings are removed. Remark: in order to be able to register key-events, TurtleScreen must have the focus. (See method listen().)

name: onkeypress
doc: Bind fun to key-press event of key if key is given, or to any key-press-event if no key is given. Remark: in order to be able to register key-events, TurtleScreen must have focus. (See method listen().)

name: onkeyrelease
doc: Bind fun to key-release event of key. If fun is None, event bindings are removed. Remark: in order to be able to register key-events, TurtleScreen must have the focus. (See method listen().)

name: onrelease
doc: Bind fun to mouse-button-release events on this turtle. If fun is None, existing bindings are removed.

name: onscreenclick
doc: Bind fun to mouse-click events on this screen. fun is called with the coordinates of the clicked point on the canvas. If fun is None, existing bindings are removed. btn is the number of the mouse button and defaults to 1, the left mouse button. If add is True, a new binding is added, otherwise it replaces a former binding.

name: ontimer
doc: Install a timer that calls fun after t milliseconds.

name: pd
doc: Lower the pen. The turtle draws a line when it moves.

name: pen
doc: Return or set the pen’s attributes in a “pen-dictionary” with the following key/value pairs:

name: pencolor
doc: Return or set the pencolor.

name: pendown
doc: Lower the pen. The turtle draws a line when it moves.

name: pensize
doc: Return or set the line thickness. If width is not given, return the current pensize. If resizemode is set to “auto” and the turtle shape is a polygon, that polygon is drawn with the same line thickness.

name: penup
doc: Lift the pen. The turtle does not draw when it moves.

name: poly
doc: Record the vertices of a polygon drawn in the with turtle.poly(): block. The first and last vertices will be connected.

name: pos
doc: Return the turtle’s current location (x,y) as a Vec2D vector.

name: position
doc: Return the turtle’s current location (x,y) as a Vec2D vector.

name: pu
doc: Lift the pen. The turtle does not draw when it moves.

name: radians
doc: Set the angle measurement units to radians. Equivalent to degrees(2 * math.pi).

name: RawPen
doc: Create a turtle. The turtle has all methods described above as “methods of Turtle/RawTurtle”.

name: RawTurtle
doc: Create a turtle. The turtle has all methods described above as “methods of Turtle/RawTurtle”.

name: register_shape
doc: Add a turtle shape to the TurtleScreen’s shape list. It can be called in four different ways:

changed.text: Added support for PNG, PGM, and PPM image formats. Both a shape name and an image file name can be specified.

name: reset
doc: Delete the turtle’s drawings and re-center the turtle. The turtle’s settings are restored to their default values.

name: resetscreen
doc: Reset all turtles on the screen to their initial state.

name: resizemode
doc: Set the resizemode to “auto”, “user” or “noresize”. If rmode is not given, return the current resizemode. The different resizemodes have the following effects:

name: right
doc: Turn the turtle right by the specified angle. The angle is measured in degrees by default; the unit can be changed with degrees() or radians(). How the heading is measured depends on the turtle mode, see mode().

name: rt
doc: Turn the turtle right by the specified angle. The angle is measured in degrees by default; the unit can be changed with degrees() or radians(). How the heading is measured depends on the turtle mode, see mode().

name: save
doc: Save the current turtle drawing (and turtles) as a PostScript file.

name: Screen
doc: Subclass of TurtleScreen, with four methods added. Calling Screen() returns the single screen object. If it does not exist yet, it is created. Otherwise the existing one is returned.

name: screensize
doc: If no arguments are given, return current (canvaswidth, canvasheight). Else resize the canvas the turtles are drawing on. Do not alter the drawing window. To observe hidden parts of the canvas, use the scrollbars. With this method, one can make visible those parts of a drawing which were outside the canvas before.

name: ScrolledCanvas
doc: Used by class Screen, which thus automatically provides a ScrolledCanvas as playground for the turtles.

name: seth
doc: Set the turtle’s heading to to_angle. Here are some common directions in degrees:

name: setheading
doc: Set the turtle’s heading to to_angle. Here are some common directions in degrees:

name: setpos
doc: Move the turtle to an absolute position. If y is None, x must be a pair of coordinates or a Vec2D, for example as returned by pos(). If the pen is down, a line is drawn. The turtle’s heading does not change.

name: setposition
doc: Move the turtle to an absolute position. If y is None, x must be a pair of coordinates or a Vec2D, for example as returned by pos(). If the pen is down, a line is drawn. The turtle’s heading does not change.

name: setundobuffer
doc: Set or disable the undo buffer. If size is an integer, an empty undo buffer of the given size is installed. size is the maximum number of turtle actions that can be undone by undo(). If size is None, the undo buffer is disabled.

name: setup
doc: Set the size and position of the main window. Default values of arguments are stored in the configuration dictionary and can be changed via a turtle.cfg file.

name: setworldcoordinates
doc: Set up a user-defined coordinate system. llx and lly are the x and y coordinates of the lower left corner of the canvas. urx and ury are the x and y coordinates of the upper right corner. Switch to mode “world” if necessary, which performs a reset. If mode “world” is already active, all drawings are redrawn according to the new coordinates. In user-defined coordinate systems, angles may appear distorted, see mode().

name: setx
doc: Set the turtle’s x coordinate to x. The y coordinate is unchanged.

name: sety
doc: Set the turtle’s y coordinate to y. The x coordinate is unchanged.

name: Shape
doc: Data structure modeling shapes. type_ is one of the strings “polygon”, “image” or “compound”. What data must be depends on type_: for “polygon” a tuple of pairs of coordinates, for “image” an image (only used internally), and for “compound” None, as a compound shape is built up using the addcomponent() method.

name: shape
doc: Set the turtle shape to the named shape. If name is not given, return the name of the current shape. The shape must exist in the TurtleScreen’s shape dictionary. Initially there are the following shapes: “arrow”, “turtle”, “circle”, “square”, “triangle” and “classic”. To add shapes, see the Screen method register_shape().

name: addcomponent
doc: Add a component to a shape of type “compound”. poly is a polygon, a tuple of pairs of numbers. fill is the color the polygon is filled with and outline is the color of its outline. If outline is not given, fill is used for it as well.

name: shapesize
doc: Return or set the turtle’s stretch factors and outline width. If no arguments are given, return the current values. Otherwise set resizemode to “user”, so that the turtle is displayed stretched according to its stretch factors:

name: shapetransform
doc: Set or return the current transformation matrix of the turtle shape.

name: shearfactor
doc: Set or return the current shearfactor. Shear the turtleshape according to the given shearfactor shear, which is the tangent of the shear angle. Do not change the turtle’s heading (direction of movement). If shear is not given: return the current shearfactor, i. e. the tangent of the shear angle, by which lines parallel to the heading of the turtle are sheared.

name: showturtle
doc: Make the turtle visible.

name: speed
doc: Return or set the turtle’s speed. If speed is not given, return the current speed. Otherwise set the turtle’s speed to an integer from 0 to 10. If speed is a number greater than 10 or smaller than 0.5, the speed is set to 0. You can also use these names instead of numbers:

name: st
doc: Make the turtle visible.

name: stamp
doc: Stamp a copy of the turtle shape onto the canvas at the current turtle position. Return a stamp_id for that stamp, which can be used to delete it by calling clearstamp(stamp_id).

name: teleport
doc: Teleport, or instantly move, the turtle to an absolute position. Unlike goto(), no line is drawn. If x or y is not given, that coordinate is kept as it is. The turtle’s heading does not change.

name: textinput
doc: Pop up a dialog window for input of a string. title is the title of the dialog window and prompt is a text describing what information to input. Return the string entered. If the dialog is canceled, return None.

name: tilt
doc: Rotate the turtleshape by angle from its current tilt-angle, but do not change the turtle’s heading (direction of movement).

name: tiltangle
doc: Set or return the current tilt-angle. If angle is given, rotate the turtleshape to point in the direction specified by angle, regardless of its current tilt-angle. Do not change the turtle’s heading (direction of movement). If angle is not given: return the current tilt-angle, i. e. the angle between the orientation of the turtleshape and the heading of the turtle (its direction of movement).

name: title
doc: Set the title of the turtle window to titlestring. The title is shown in the title bar of the turtle graphics window.

name: towards
doc: Return the angle of the line from the turtle’s position to (x,y). If y is None, x must be a pair of coordinates, a Vec2D, for example as returned by pos(), or another turtle. The angle is measured from the turtle’s start orientation, which depends on the turtle mode, see mode().

name: tracer
doc: Turn turtle animation on or off and set the drawing delay. If n is given, only every n-th regular screen update is performed, which can be used to speed up the drawing of complex graphics. If n is 0, animation is turned off and the screen is only updated by calling update(). If delay is given, it sets the drawing delay, see delay(). When called without arguments, return the current value of n.

name: Turtle
doc: Subclass of RawTurtle, has the same interface but draws on a default Screen object created automatically when needed for the first time.

name: TurtleGraphicsError
doc: Raised for invalid arguments or operations. For example, a malformed color string:

name: turtles
doc: Return the list of turtles on the screen.

name: TurtleScreen
doc: Provides screen oriented methods like bgcolor() etc. that are described above.

name: turtlesize
doc: Return or set the turtle’s stretch factors and outline width. If no arguments are given, return the current values. Otherwise set resizemode to “user”, so that the turtle is displayed stretched according to its stretch factors:

name: undo
doc: Undo (repeatedly) the last turtle action(s). Number of available undo actions is determined by the size of the undobuffer.

name: undobufferentries
doc: Return the number of entries in the undo buffer.

name: up
doc: Lift the pen. The turtle does not draw when it moves.

name: update
doc: Perform a TurtleScreen update. To be used when tracer is turned off.

name: Vec2D
doc: A two-dimensional vector class, used as a helper class for implementing turtle graphics. May be useful for turtle graphics programs too. Derived from tuple, so a vector is a tuple!

name: width
doc: Return or set the line thickness. If width is not given, return the current pensize. If resizemode is set to “auto” and the turtle shape is a polygon, that polygon is drawn with the same line thickness.

name: window_height
doc: Return the height of the turtle window.

name: window_width
doc: Return the width of the turtle window.

name: write
doc: Write text - the string representation of arg - at the current turtle position according to align (“left”, “center” or “right”) and with the given font. If move is true, the pen is moved to the bottom-right corner of the text. By default, move is False.

name: write_docstringdict
doc: Create and write docstring-dictionary to a Python script with the given filename. This function has to be called explicitly (it is not used by the turtle graphics classes). The docstring dictionary will be written to the Python script filename.py. It is intended to serve as a template for translation of the docstrings into different languages.

name: xcor
doc: Return the turtle’s x coordinate.

name: ycor
doc: Return the turtle’s y coordinate.
